summary: This tadabbur lecture on 20 Ramadan at Masjid Sentosa links Surah Al-Alaq and Surah Al-Qadr with the angel Jibril. The ustaz recalls the first ten verses of Al-Alaq, including man's transgression and Abu Jahal who tried to stamp on the Prophet's neck during prostration but retreated because he saw fire and wings. He then tells of three of the Prophet's encounters with Jibril: the opening of his chest at Banu Sa'd, the first revelation, and Jibril coming as a man in white clothes asking about Islam, faith, ihsan and the Hour. The lecture closes with Surah Al-Qadr: a night better than a thousand months, when angels and the Spirit descend in numbers greater than the sand, and encouragement to seek the odd nights.
keyPoints: People who feel they have wealth and power tend to transgress, but all will return to Allah.
Abu Jahal retreated when about to stamp on the prostrating Prophet SAW because he saw fire and wings, which was Jibril.
Jibril came as a man in white clothes and asked about Islam, faith, ihsan and the signs of the Hour.
Laylat al-Qadr is better than a thousand months, and the angels and the Spirit descend in greater numbers than sand.
The Prophet SAW woke his family in the last ten nights of Ramadan and told people to seek the odd nights.

chapters.title: Opening on 20 Ramadan
chapters.summary: The ustaz continues the sirah class at Masjid Sentosa as we chase Laylat al-Qadr.

chapters.title: Masjid Sentosa and the plan
chapters.summary: Sentosa means peace. The ustaz plans to read Al-Alaq to verse 10 and tell of Abu Jahal, which links to Jibril.

chapters.title: The meaning of Bismillah
chapters.summary: Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim are better translated as the Most Compassionate and Most Merciful.

chapters.title: Recap of the first four verses
chapters.summary: The ustaz repeats read in the Lord's name, man from alaq, the Generous Lord and the pen.

chapters.title: Allah's blessings and Gaza
chapters.summary: Festive clothes, cakes and the safety of the mosque are provision from the Generous Allah, while remembering our brothers in Gaza.

chapters.title: Man transgresses
chapters.summary: When he sees himself with wealth and power, man turns wicked and transgresses.

chapters.title: All will return to Allah
chapters.summary: We will return to Allah through death, and this world is only a temporary stop.

chapters.title: Abu Jahal prevents prayer
chapters.summary: Allah asks about the one who forbids a servant from praying, and Abu Jahal threatened to stamp on the Prophet's neck.

chapters.title: Abu Jahal retreats
chapters.summary: As he was about to stamp, Abu Jahal retreated in fear and said he saw fire and wings lunging at him.

chapters.title: The first meeting with Jibril
chapters.summary: The ustaz recalls the opening of his chest at Banu Sa'd at age three and its stitch mark.

chapters.title: Jibril in white clothes
chapters.summary: Jibril came as a man in clean white clothes with no trace of travel, sitting knee to knee with the Prophet SAW.

chapters.title: Islam, faith, ihsan and the Hour
chapters.summary: Jibril asked about Islam, faith, ihsan and the signs of the Hour, and confirmed the Prophet's answers.

chapters.title: Surah Al-Qadr
chapters.summary: Allah sent down the Quran on Laylat al-Qadr, a night both powerful and crowded.

chapters.title: Better than a thousand months
chapters.summary: Allah asks what would make you know that night, for it is better than a thousand months, over 83 years.

chapters.title: The angels and the Spirit descend
chapters.summary: Angels descend in greater numbers than sand with Jibril to see who is doing good, and the night is full of peace.

chapters.title: Seeking the odd nights
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW woke his family and told people to seek it in the odd nights of the last ten.

dalil.translation: Read! Your Lord is the Most Bountiful One
who taught by [means of] the pen,

dalil.context: Surely to your Lord is the return.
dalil.translation: [Prophet], all will return to your Lord.

dalil.translation: We sent it down on the Night of Glory.

dalil.context: Allah asks what could make you know what Laylat al-Qadr is.
dalil.translation: What will explain to you what that Night of Glory is?

dalil.context: Laylat al-Qadr is better than a thousand months.
dalil.translation: The Night of Glory is better than a thousand months;

dalil.context: The angels and the Spirit descend by permission of their Lord.

dalil.translation: [there is] peace that night until the break of dawn.
Jibril came in the form of a man in white clothes and asked the Prophet SAW about Islam, faith, ihsan and the signs of the Hour, then confirmed his answers.
dalil.context: The ustaz relates this story, explaining the Prophet's answers. He does not name a narrator or source.

dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW said to seek Laylat al-Qadr in the last ten nights of Ramadan, on the odd nights.
dalil.context: The ustaz mentions the Prophet's encouragement to seek that night. He does not name a narrator or source.

people.context: Threatened to stamp on the Prophet's neck while he prostrated but retreated in fear.
Protected the Prophet SAW from Abu Jahal, opened his chest at Banu Sa'd and asked about Islam in human form.

people.role: Wet nurse of the Prophet SAW
people.context: Returned him to Aminah after the opening of his chest.
Mentioned as one of the prophets Jibril met.

sirah.era: After the first revelation: reflecting on Al-Alaq and Al-Qadr
sirah.summary: This lecture links verses of Al-Alaq and Al-Qadr with the Prophet's meetings with Jibril and Laylat al-Qadr.

events.label: Chest
events.title: His chest is opened
events.desc: At age three Jibril opened his chest and washed his heart with zamzam water.

events.label: Abu Jahal
events.title: Abu Jahal wants to stamp on him
events.desc: Abu Jahal retreated, seeing fire and wings coming to protect him.

events.label: Jibril's hadith
events.title: Jibril asks about Islam
events.desc: Jibril came as a man in white and questioned the Prophet SAW.

events.label: Al-Qadr
events.title: Surah Al-Qadr is recited
events.desc: The ustaz explains the night better than a thousand months.

lessons.title: Giving thanks for the Generous Allah's blessings
lessons.body: Festive clothes, cakes and a feeling of safety in the mosque are all provision from Allah.

lessons.title: Power and wealth can make people transgress
lessons.body: Those who feel they have enough wealth and power readily oppress others.

lessons.title: We will return to Allah
lessons.body: This world is only a temporary stop for testing before returning to Allah.

lessons.title: Not obstructing people from worship
lessons.body: Allah condemns those who forbid a servant from praying, like Abu Jahal.

lessons.title: Allah protects His Messenger
lessons.body: Jibril came to protect the Prophet SAW so that Abu Jahal retreated.

lessons.title: Ihsan in worship
lessons.body: Worship as if you see Allah, and if you cannot, remember that Allah sees you.

lessons.title: Laylat al-Qadr is better than a thousand months
lessons.body: Worship on that night equals more than 83 years.

lessons.title: Reviving the nights with family
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW woke his family to read Quran, pray and make prayers and to feed the poor.

lessons.title: Not overeating
lessons.body: Do not eat too much so that you can rise for worship on the odd nights.
